content_html:
Luno is a cryptocurrency exchange and wallet, founded in 2013 and led by co-founder and chief executive Marcus Swanepoel, that serves countries with high crypto adoption including South Africa, Nigeria, Indonesia and Malaysia. In 2020 the US-based Digital Currency Group acquired the exchange, having invested in its 2014 seed round.

In Nigeria

Luno began serving Nigeria in 2016 and started physical operations in 2017, according to a Techpoint Africa feature. Customers can buy bitcoin and ethereum with naira using local bank cards and domestic transfers, and the exchange has naira trading pairs that let users convert crypto back to naira and withdraw it to a bank account.

Who is behind it

Digital Currency Group, founded by Barry Silbert in 2015, is an investment company focused on digital currencies and decentralised technologies. Silbert said he was proud to have supported Luno as an early investor when the acquisition was announced.

Taking care when buying crypto

  • Prices move sharply, so invest only what you can afford to lose.
  • Turn on two-factor authentication and protect the email account tied to the exchange.
  • Read fee tables for buying, selling and withdrawing in naira before you trade.
  • Keep records of transactions, since tax treatment of crypto differs by country.

What we could not verify

We did not trade on Luno. Nigerian rules on crypto change, so check the latest regulator guidance and the exchange's own terms before depositing money.
